title: Keto vs Paleo
shortAnswer: The ketogenic diet is a very high-fat, very low-carb diet (under 50g carbs/day) that puts the body in ketosis. The paleo diet focuses on eating like our Paleolithic ancestors — whole foods, no processed items, no grains or legumes. Both eliminate grains and sugar.
verdict: Keto is more medically researched for weight loss and epilepsy. Paleo is more sustainable long-term and less restrictive. Both are effective for weight management.

lines.hook: Under 50 grams of carbs a day. That's one banana and you're done.
lines.tape: Keto is a metabolic switch. Paleo is a grocery list. Very different levels of strict.
rounds: Keto puts a hard ceiling on carbs. Paleo just deletes grains and moves on.
Seventy to eighty percent of your calories from fat. Fat becomes the fuel.
Paleo lets you eat an apple. On keto, fruit is a budget item.
Both diets throw out beans and lentils. Nobody wins this one.
Keto has clinical backing for epilepsy and weight loss. Paleo's evidence is thinner.
lines.verdict: Keto takes it 3-1 on the numbers. Pick paleo if you want something you'll still be doing next year.

youtubeTitle: Keto vs Paleo: Which Diet Actually Holds Up?
youtubeDescription:
A head-to-head breakdown of the ketogenic diet versus the paleo diet on carb limits, fat intake, fruit and legumes, and research evidence. Keto wins on points thanks to stronger clinical backing, but paleo is the less restrictive option for the long haul.

Figures accurate as of August 2026. Statistics change over time — see the full, maintained comparison at https://www.aversusb.net/compare/keto-vs-paleo
